articles.title: The Walls Don't Talk: How Stalefish Builds
articles.excerpt: The line came out of an essay about the app Cairn, at the end of a paragraph about visual restraint, and it was meant to stay there. The walls don't talk. Cairn is a room; you walk through it and noti…
articles.body: The line came out of an essay about the app Cairn, at the end of a paragraph about visual restraint, and it was meant to stay there. The walls don't talk. Cairn is a room; you walk through it and notice what's there, and the walls carry color and texture and they don't address you. I wrote it to describe one app. Then I looked at the other things the studio has built and found it describing all of them. So this piece is the moment of noticing the shape. Four principles run underneath everything Stalefish makes. None of them came from a manifesto. They surfaced one product at a time, one problem at a time, and they turned out to agree with each other before anyone set out to name them. Naming them is the whole job here. Classification without interpretation. Ambient over declarative.
articles.author: Stalefish Labs

articles.title: On this day in space! Sept. 4, 1962: NASA's Mariner 2 spacecrafts performs the 1st-ever maneuver in deep space so it could reach Venus
articles.excerpt: On Sept. 4, 1962, NASA's Mariner 2 spacecraft performed the first-ever rocket maneuver in deep space as it did a quick mid-course correction on its way to Venus. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Sept. 4, 1962, NASA's Mariner 2 spacecraft performed the first-ever rocket maneuver in deep space as it did a quick mid-course correction on its way to Venus. It had launched just eight days earlier and needed to burn its engines to ensure that its trajectory would take it to Venus . The midcourse maneuver was necessary because the Atlas-Agena rocket that launched Mariner 2 didn't launch with enough accuracy to get the trajectory right in one shot. When it was about 1.5 million miles (2.4 million km) from Earth , it fired its engines to help steer it in the right direction. The entire maneuver required five separate commands sent from mission control, telling the spacecraft to roll, pitch, turn and burn its motor.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: Hubble Telescope sees spectacular 'superbubble' | Space photo of the day for Sept. 4, 2026
articles.excerpt: The Hubble Space Telescope has spotted a spectacular 'super bubble' in our Milky Way's nearest neighbor the Large Magellanic Cloud. Check out our space photo of the day.
articles.body: This nebula is named LHA 120-N44, or N44 for short, and it’s located in the constellation Dorado. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. Gouliermis) About 160,000 light-years away lies one of our Milky Way's little galactic neighbors: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). And thanks to a new observing program, the Hubble Space Telescope has provided us with an intricate image of a nebula in the LMC. The surprising part? There's a giant void at the center. Scientists call it a "superbubble." What is it? What you're seeing in this image is a nebula within the LMC known as LHA 120-N44, or simply N44. It's located in the constellation of Dorado and, like a classic nebula, is the site of stars being born at a noticeably rapid rate.

articles.title: SmallRig brings modular mounting to portable power with its new Nano Power Bank series

articles.body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority Most consumer power banks are designed to sit in a pocket or a bag until you need to plug something in. That’s great if you only need to charge your phone, but these don’t work as well when you’re trying to run a camera, a wireless mic, and a monitor off the same battery during a long shoot. There’s rarely a clean way to attach the power bank itself, so you often end up improvising with cable ties, tape, or Velcro straps. The Nano Power Bank series addresses this problem directly. The two models – the Nano 36 and the Nano 72 – in the lineup come with built-in 1/4″-20 threaded holes and dedicated V-mount plates, so they can be attached to camera cages, tripods, gimbals, and other accessories in SmallRig’s existing ecosystem.

articles.title: How did the infant sun form? Scientists get surprising new insights from 4.6-billion-year-old space dust
articles.excerpt: New research suggests that dust from meteorites contains a "fossil record" dating back 4.6 billion years to the formation of the sun, revealing the role magnetism played in the birth of the solar syst…
articles.body: New research suggests that dust from meteorites contains a "fossil record" dating back to the formation of the sun. The research reveals that magnetism played a far greater role in the birth of the solar system than had previously been suspected. Around 4.6 billion years ago, the solar system was a cloud of gas and dust, known as a solar nebula. Over the next few million years, this cloud began to flatten, forming a donut-shaped ring or torus with a budding star gathering mass at its core. Eventually, planets would form within this so-called protoplanetary disk. Scientists have always theorized that gravity was the main sculptor during this early era. But the new study suggests that gravity had major assistance from magnetism.

articles.title: Scientists watch a comet being born 3 billion miles away
articles.excerpt: A rare look at a centaur transforming into a comet with coma is providing a missing link in the evolution of small, icy solar system bodies.
articles.body: Astronomers have witnessed a small, icy body that orbits the sun out beyond Jupiter transforming into a comet, providing a missing link between comets and inert bodies called centaurs. The object in question is called 450P/LONEOS and is named after the Lowell Observatory survey that found it back in 2004. It is a centaur, which is a breed of inactive body that orbits the sun between Jupiter and Neptune . These objects are thought to have wandered in from the Kuiper Belt beyond Pluto , their paths perhaps perturbed by distant gravitational interactions with the gas giant planets, or even a nudge from a passing star . Because a given centaur's orbit crosses the path of at least one of Jupiter, Saturn , Uranus and Neptune, a centaur's orbit is unstable over millions of years.

articles.title: 'Alien: Isolation 2': Facing a ruthless and evolved Xenomorph in our Gamescom hands-on preview
articles.excerpt: Sega and Creative Assembly's long-awaited survival horror sequel hits the ground running with a new cast of characters and a fast-paced prologue.
articles.body: It's hard to downplay excitement for Alien: Isolation 2 after a first menacing teaser and promising early previews. Alien video games are in a good spot right now thanks to bangers like Aliens Dark Descent and Fireteam Elite 2, but nothing has hit quite like Creative Assembly's 2014 survival horror classic. Now, after a thrilling Gamescom hands-on demo, it looks like the studio has nailed it once again, bringing Xenomorph -shaped scares to the next generation. At least that's what its breezy prologue section I played at Gamescom suggests. As the earliest possible section of the game, no new mechanics were present, and the larger ideas and structure are still a big mystery.
